title: Answer to Question: The Dollar Crisis and the Rise in the Prices of Oil, Metals and Foodstuffs
text:
Answer to Question
The Dollar Crisis and the Rise in the Prices of Oil, Metals and Foodstuffs

Question: The dollar crisis is still continuing, as it is in a striking decline, and that has been followed by a rise in the prices of oil, gold and other metals, and then that has also been followed by a rise in the prices of foodstuffs. All of that has happened as a precedent the like of which has not happened before, in terms of its continuation and severity, and its encompassing several crises...

So is this crisis the result of an actual economic problem, or is it the hands of American politics that have moved it and escalated it?

I hope you will clarify that, and may Allah reward you with good.

Answer:

This problem has a real economic side, but political hands have entered onto this line which escalated the problem, widened its course, and made it take on this size that we see.

So that the picture becomes completely clear, we shall explain how the crisis arose, how the political games entered it, then how it affected the rise in the prices of oil, gold and metals, and then the emergence of the food crisis.

First: There is a real crisis in the American economy which has affected the effectiveness and strength of the dollar, and consequently this severe decline befell it. This crisis arose through the following causes:

The American trade deficit

America imports more goods and services than it exports. The appetite of the American consumer is open to importing. For example, in 2003 CE America imported goods and services worth $1,652 billion, while its exports equalled $1,203 billion, that is, the trade deficit was 449 billion dollars, and this deficit escalated until it reached 816 billion dollars. The difference between what was imported and what was exported consisted of printed American papers (dollars) or American government bonds, and this naturally leads to an actual decline in the dollar, even if it is not officially announced.

America had not passed through such a trade deficit. On the contrary, America passed through a trade surplus for many decades, especially after the Second World War. Then this surplus began to decrease... especially because of competition from the European and Asian countries, which produce goods at lower prices, which increased the American consumer's import of goods and services from those countries. Then this phenomenon coincided with the size of military expenditure on the Vietnamese war, which led to raising the bill of payments, and consequently America was compelled in 1971 to cancel the backing of the dollar with gold; this was the first of the shocks. In the eighties, when world trade grew and factories moved from America to countries with cheap labour, the appearance of the economic deficit increased. Likewise, importing steadily from the countries exporting cheap goods, such as Mexico, China and Malaysia, led to the widening of the trade gap.

Thus the deficit in the trade balance and the balance of payments created doubts and lack of confidence in the American economy among investors, and later led to the fall of the dollar.

Indebtedness: The statistics of the American Treasury Department showed the rise of government debts (the central administration and the local administrations) from 4.3 trillion dollars in 1990 to 8.4 trillion dollars in 2003 and to 8.9 trillion dollars in 2007. These public debts have come to constitute 64% of the gross domestic product. Thereby the United States can be classified among the states that suffer severely from their public debts. The weight of American indebtedness does not stop at the government administrations but includes individuals and companies as well. Individual debts recently reached an amount of 6.6 trillion dollars. As for the debts of companies, they occupy first place in terms of their size, amounting to 18.4 trillion dollars. Thereby the overall total is about 34 trillion dollars, that is, three times the gross domestic product. These debts are in themselves a dangerous economic crisis.

The rise of the euro:

Since the euro was minted, the euro has become the second world reserve after the dollar. The euro inherited this standing from the German mark, and indeed increased its standing, and that was at the expense of the dollar. Thus confidence in the euro has been increasing while for the dollar it has been decreasing, and all of this affected the demand for the dollar, so its value fell. And the dollar's loss of its value pushed many investors to adopt the euro in their investments instead of the dollar.

In addition to that, America suffers from other economic problems, foremost among them inflation, which has exceeded 4%, unemployment, which constitutes 5%, industry, which is retreating, and poverty and poor educational services...

All these factors led to the decline in the value of the dollar.

This decline led some central banks to deliberately reduce their stock of dollars.

Paul Mackel, a currency strategist at the «HSBC» bank, says that the central banks «realised some time ago that they do not wish for an excessive increase in what they own of dollars. The total holdings of the central banks around the world held in the form of dollars has fallen from 73 percent to 64 percent».

This is the real economic basis of the dollar crisis.

Second: After that, the American political hands entered into moving the crisis to serve their interests, and to transfer the crisis from a local American crisis to an international crisis... And that was as follows:

1- The decline in the currency of the exporting country increases its exports, because the prices of goods become relatively cheap, since importers will pay a lower monetary value, considering that the prices of those materials in the currency of their country have become lower as a result of the decline of the currency. For example, if the importer was paying $(1000) as the price of the commodity, and it was equal to (1000) euros for example, then if the dollar declined by (10)% for example, the importer would pay (900) euros instead of the previous $(1000). For this reason traders turn to importing that country's goods because of the decline of its currency.

However, this is good if the decline does not exceed 5%, and it is acceptable up to 10%. But if it increases beyond that, it will form a burden on the producing factories because of the inflation resulting from the devaluation, that is, the increase in the prices of materials in that country as a result of the devaluation of its currency, since its purchasing power decreases.

Because of this inflation, the cost increases for the factories, so the prices of their exported products increase; that is, the price of the commodity will not remain $(1000), for example, but will increase. Thus the decline of the currency, if it increases beyond a reasonable limit, will increase the cost of production, so the price of the commodity increases, and consequently the quantity of exports decreases because of the inflation resulting from the devaluation. In America's case, the decline of the dollar has exceeded the reasonable limit. For example, the euro has come to exceed 1.6 dollars, after it was equal in 2000 CE to about $0.8; that is, the decline of the dollar has exceeded the maximum economic limits by more than five times...

For this reason American exports, as a result of this devaluation, increased only by a slight amount; that is, the trade deficit, although it decreased a little, remained present.

Nevertheless, America did not take a measure to correct this deficit. It did not bring out part of its oil stock for use in order to reduce the price of energy for the producing factories, so that the cost of production would decrease and exports increase. Rather, the Bush administration refused to bring out part of its oil stock and put it to use to reduce the price of energy, which had escalated greatly; that is, it did not treat the subject of the trade deficit economically.

Likewise it did not treat the indebtedness; rather, it worked to increase it because of the continuation of its criminal aggression on Afghanistan and Iraq, which costs it more than (2) trillion dollars. Also, the Bush administration gave loans to the rich American capitalists of about a trillion dollars through cutting taxes for them, for political and electoral motives..., which kept the indebtedness as it was and increasing.

Thus America kept the dollar devalued and did not take any economic measure to correct it. Then it used this devaluation politically, by blackmailing the states with large reserves of the dollar..., such as China, which owns a dollar reserve of about a thousand billion dollars, which makes it lose enormous sums as a result of the devaluation, then India, the European states and the oil states... This forced those states to try to prop up the dollar by floating some of their currencies, and buying the dollar, that is, increasing the demand for it, so that they reduce its decline somewhat...

2- Then the next American political step was in the face of the collapse of the shares of the mortgage companies, by means of which America was able to transfer the crisis from an American crisis to an international crisis!

The state had provided loans at reduced interest to the companies working in housing, especially the mortgage companies, which sell homes in exchange for mortgaging them until the instalments of the sale price are paid. For this reason liquidity became abundantly available to these companies, which pushed them to ease the conditions for selling homes..., and at easy, indeed reduced, prices, since the material liquidity of the companies working in housing and mortgages had become available through the loans provided by the state at reduced interest... So the people in America turned to buying homes... and the ways were opened before them to pay the first instalment from easy loans they take from the American banks, which began giving loans to home owners at suitable interest; indeed, they give housing loans for the full price of the mortgaged home, and not as the European banks do, giving a loan within the limits of 60% of the price of the mortgaged property. All of that was because the state was giving loans to the companies and banks at reduced interest, which made the property sector flourish noticeably.

Because of the policy of globalisation and the companies' opening up to one another whenever they find prosperity and profit, the international companies, the private and central banks, and likewise individuals turned to buying shares in the American mortgage companies in pursuit of profit..., as the values of properties, and consequently the shares of property companies listed on the stock exchange, began rising continuously in all parts of the world, especially in the United States, until buying property became the best type of investment, while other activities, including modern technology, were exposed to loss, as happened previously when the turn towards investment in the field of information and communications technology was intense. Americans, individuals and companies, turned to buying properties for the purpose of residence, long-term investment or speculation. The property facilities expanded to the degree that the banks granted loans even to individuals unable to repay their debts because of their weak incomes.

This matter continued without problems until last year, especially when the burden of debts on the state increased. America stopped giving easy loans to the mortgage companies and the banks, and indeed demanded that they repay the loans they had taken previously when they fell due... The mortgage companies and the banks began demanding from the home owners, and given the unemployment, inflation and the bad economic situation in America, the home owners were unable to pay either the sale price or the loans for the instalments which they had taken from the banks... The value of properties fell, and individuals were no longer able to repay their debts even after selling their mortgaged properties. The house that was worth half a million dollars came to be valued at 200 thousand, and no one is found to buy it, as came in the news. More than two million Americans lost their property ownership and became shackled with financial obligations for the rest of their lives. As a result of the harm to the creditor banks because the borrowers did not repay their loans, the values of their shares on the stock exchange fell, and the mortgage companies suffered heavy losses estimated at two thousand billion dollars, and numerous property companies announced their bankruptcy.

Consequently, much of the debt became bad debt that cannot be recovered.

In a review of the major banks which were recently exposed to a violent shock in the American mortgage sector, the periodical magazine «Souq», issued by the Arab-German Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Berlin, pointed to the American bank «Citigroup», which revealed at the start of the new year its losses in the last quarter of the past year, amounting to 9.83 billion dollars (6.6 billion euros at the time), and the loss of the mentioned bank in the property field has risen until now to more than 18.1 billion dollars.

The same negative development took place with the American bank «Merrill Lynch», which announced writing off 14.1 billion dollars of its assets, which means that its losses for the last quarter of 2007 in turn reached 9.8 billion dollars, the biggest loss in its history.

And the same thing happened with the giant Swiss bank «UBS», which obtained billions of dollars from the Singapore sovereign fund (GIC) to avoid bankruptcy.

Thus the shares of the property companies collapsed on the stock exchange, and consequently the shares of companies and banks fell in many countries of the world, as they had a connection with investment or shares in the American property companies or with direct business in the American property sector. Even the contagion struck the sectors that do not deal in property activities; but because of globalisation and the intertwining of the business of the economic sectors, they were affected.

No sooner had the values of shares fallen on Wall Street in America than the general index of values fell by 7.1% in Frankfurt, 6.8% in Paris, 5.4% in London, 7.5% in Madrid, 3.8% in Tokyo, 5.1% in Shanghai, 6% in São Paulo, 9.8% in Riyadh, 9.4% in Dubai, 3% in Beirut and 4.2% in Cairo.

Because of the magnitude of the loss and the size of the bad debts, it was decided that the French President Nicolas Sarkozy and the British Prime Minister Gordon Brown would urge the banks, at their meeting on 27/03/2008 CE, to make a full and immediate disclosure of the bad debts they hold. Brown had said in January last that Britain faces a harsh test with a world economy in a difficult and dangerous situation because of the credit crisis resulting from the American mortgage loan crisis. That came after Northern Rock, the fifth British banking institution in the sector of lending related to mortgages, was exposed to severe harm because of the repercussions of the mortgage crisis in the United States.

Thus America transferred the crisis of the mortgage companies from an American crisis to an international crisis, to the degree that the central banks in Europe pumped more than 150 billion dollars last year to support the mortgage companies, so that the stock exchanges of the world, Europe among them, would not be harmed by them and collapse, because of the extension of the international companies in all countries and their interlocking with one another due to the system of globalisation. By that America blackmailed Europe and supported its companies, that is, the American mortgage companies, by this means.

In conclusion, the American crisis has several dimensions, economic and political. America is passing through real crises which led to the decline of the dollar, so it carried out political manoeuvres or (conspiracies) to make the whole world share with it in its crises, otherwise the whole world would drown with it, especially after the spread of globalisation and the opening of all markets to one another under the name of the market economy, and the extension of all the companies across the world and their intertwining with one another. Most of the countries of the world, with their markets, have become open to one another.

Thus America exploited the decline of its dollar due to its economic crisis to lighten its trade deficit and for political blackmail, especially regarding the states which have a large stock of dollars. Likewise it was able to transfer the crisis of the mortgage companies into an international crisis, and it is not far from this crisis.

Nevertheless, all these American political actions will not return the American economy to its prosperity; rather, they may only stop its collapse. Were it not for the policy of globalisation and the open market, and were it not for the capitalist economic system controlling the economy of the world... and were it not that states still adopt the dollar as a central reserve, were it not for that, the American economy would not have remained standing on its feet until now.

Third: As for the cause of the rise in the prices of mineral products such as oil, gold, iron...: after the collapse of the mortgage companies, the decline of the market of shares and bonds, and the decline of the stock exchange indices, the confidence of investors decreased in the means of investment that do not have intrinsic value, that is, which do not carry their own intrinsic value, such as bonds, shares and stock exchanges. So the investors turned away from them to means of investment with intrinsic value, such as gold and other important metals, and this is what increased the demand for gold, so its price rose enormously, the price of gold reaching $1000, and it is a candidate to rise to about $1500 or more according to the current circumstances...

The ones most harmed by the rise in the prices of gold are the United States, since this matter, if it continues, will return the dollar to a value worth no more than the value of the paper and the writing on it. For this reason it is likely that America will in the coming period curb the prices of gold. Signs of that have begun to appear, as the International Monetary Fund took a decision to sell 403 tonnes of gold because of the budget deficit; however, the International Monetary Fund announced that it would carry out that sale in widely spaced, long-term periods. This announcement is a (speculative) announcement that would affect lowering the price of gold. There is a possibility that the gold will be sold to the central banks, which may cause the central banks to raise the interest rate, which would cause raising the exchange rate. And again, the statements of the International Monetary Fund on 09 April 2008 that the financial crisis will cost a trillion dollars were, more than being an explanation of the reality with fairness and truthfulness, tantamount to speculation to change the direction of the course of the economy and finance. As came in a commentary carried by the English newspaper the Telegraph, the International Monetary Fund is the last address that can be knocked on to get out of the existing financial crisis. Therefore this statement is tantamount to a preparation for that.

Thus the fall in the value of the dollar and the crisis of the loss of investors' confidence in the market of American assets pushed many investors not to invest in fiduciary paper money. The rational assessment of this is that the current paper money is not backed wholly by tangible assets. That is, in this atmosphere the transfer of the crisis of confidence spreads rapidly to the rest of the currencies. For this reason some central banks, such as the Chinese central bank, began buying gold, which led to the rise of the price of gold to its highest levels. And this is the same cause of the rise in the prices of some metals such as silver and platinum.

Also, the increase in the demand of India and China for copper, zinc, aluminium and nickel has led to an increase in their prices, and this demand for these metals from India and China is because of the accelerating growth of the economy of the two countries. This demand for these metals has continued for 12 years from China and the last 4 years from India. China has spent $1 trillion on infrastructure and will spend an additional $50 billion every year for the next fifteen years. India began rebuilding its infrastructure six years ago. The beginning of the investments was weak, but the volume of investments in the last four years reached $50 billion, and a plan has been set to invest between $30-$40 billion annually for the next ten years. However, there are not enough metals to cover this plan. In addition to that, the rise in the prices of petroleum has increased the cost of production and consequently increased the rise of prices in general.

The cause of the rise in the prices of oil goes back to a fall in the value of the dollar, and an increase in the purchasing power for oil on the part of states such as the European Union, China and India, to meet the increase in demand for it in order to meet the need of those countries for oil. However, the important cause which led to the rise in the price of oil is speculation. America's speculations on oil led to the rise of its prices, so that the dollars present in the market would be collected from those who seek to buy oil, so that America can avoid the collapse of its currency. And this is the reason for the lack of firmness of the information about the American oil stock.

Speculation has a role in raising prices; for example, speculation in futures contracts in oil increased. Likewise speculation in the prices of metals, at their head gold. The rise in the prices of gold is attributed to the turn of states such as China, Russia and some Asian states to buying gold to rid themselves of the enormous quantities of dollars they hold. The states no longer trust the dollar, and its decline causes them heavy losses. Likewise China's turn to buying iron and the rest of the metals necessary for industry, which increased the prices of iron and the other metals. Here in Germany, for example, there came to be a great demand for scrap iron, and its prices rose, indeed doubled, because much of it began to be exported to China.

It is known that whenever the dollar falls, the price of oil rises, in an inverse relationship known for a long time, and this is the reality of the situation today. On 17/04/2008 CE oil prices registered levels that crossed the threshold of 115 dollars per barrel, then continued rising until they exceeded today, 5/5/2008 CE, the amount of 120 dollars.

Thus the prices of oil have risen to more than four times their level since 2002, as demand increased, especially in China and the rest of the emerging economies, and expectations indicate that prices will reach 130 dollars at the end of the coming month of December.

Fourth: As for the world food crisis: in the shadow of the worsening of the world economic crisis brought about by the American mortgage crisis, another crisis of greater danger has resulted, threatening world food security. In all parts of the world, the prices of foods have risen, from bread to milk.

The crisis appeared during the recent period after the rise in the prices of wheat, maize, rice and the rest of the basic foodstuffs in the recent years, and it escalated at an alarming pace in the last few months.

On 6/12/2008 CE the British magazine The Economist published a report in which it came that the prices of grains have risen in an unprecedented manner since the founding of The Economist's index of food prices in 1945; the increase according to The Economist reached 75%. As for the exchange of the Chicago Board of Trade, which represents the first world measure regarding the prices of grains in the world, it mentioned that wheat rose in price by 90%, soybeans 80%, maize 20%, and prices are still rising from that date until today.

As for the causes of the rise in prices, and consequently the occurrence of the food crisis, the most prominent of them are:

1- The rise in the prices of oil and the decline in the prices of the dollar:

The rise in the prices of oil led to a rise in the prices of agricultural requirements such as seeds, fertiliser, pesticides, machinery and transport. The rise in the cost of production and transport affected the rise in the prices of foodstuffs, especially wheat, rice and maize. For example, the price of rice in the Philippines rose by 70% during the last year.

This is from one side; and from another side, the prices of foodstuffs are mostly valued in dollars, so when the value of the dollar declined, prices rose automatically.

Graziano said: «The absence of confidence in the dollar made the investment funds search for higher returns in primary commodities... first in metals, then in foods». Many speculators in the last five years transferred their money to the markets of primary commodities in search of higher returns than they obtain from the markets of shares and bonds.

2- Climatic conditions: which affect the reduction of agricultural production, such as floods and hurricanes, then drought. For example, one of the largest exporters of grains, Australia, is facing the most dangerous cases of drought in its history... In recent years these climatic conditions were accompanied by an economic boom in some states such as China, India and Brazil, which led to an increase in the consumption of meat.

It is known that to produce a piece of meat containing one hundred calories, the animals producing the meat must be fed 700 calories of grains. And of the 2.13 billion tonnes of grains, only 1.01 billion tonnes are allocated to feeding people, according to the statistics of the Food and Agriculture Organisation of the United Nations. Consequently, raising livestock increases the rise of world prices.

3- The production of biofuel from grains:

Jean Ziegler, the United Nations Special Rapporteur on the right to food, considered in a statement to a German radio station that the intensive production of biofuel today represents "a crime against humanity" because of its effect on the rise of the prices of foodstuffs in the world.

Biofuel is based on agricultural products, and in recent years many industrial states have used agricultural crops and agricultural lands in producing biofuel to lighten dependence on oil, whose prices have risen to record figures. This led to an increase in demand for biofuel, and consequently the rise of the prices of grains.

In countries such as the United States and Brazil, agricultural lands were converted to growing maize and soybeans for producing ethanol. Since 2001 the quantity of maize used in producing bio-ethanol in the United States has increased by 300%. America also seeks to produce 35 billion gallons (133 billion litres) of ethanol by 2017. The American Congress approved, in the Energy document of 2005, increasing the production of ethanol extracted from maize from 4 billion gallons in 2006 to 7.5 in 2012.

In March 2007 the American President "George Bush" met his Brazilian counterpart "Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva" to sign a treaty between the two countries, the "ethanol treaty", for joint cooperation between the two countries to conduct research and develop the next generation of biofuel production, and to form a trade union for biofuel, especially in the countries of Central Asia. The "ethanol" agreement between the two presidents was the beginning of the growth of the phenomenon of growing grains in order to use them in producing biofuel. The plantations of sugar cane, palm oil and soya designated for producing biofuel have wiped out grasslands and forests in Brazil, Argentina, Colombia, Ecuador and Uruguay. Soya plantations in Brazil have occupied 21 million hectares of forest lands, and 14 million hectares in Argentina, and it does not appear that this phenomenon will recede as long as grain prices are rising. 100 million tonnes of grains will be cut from the total of 2.13 billion tonnes for the extraction of biofuel in 2008; in other words, these tonnes will be used to feed cars.

4- Administrative and political failure:

As for the production of wheat, which is considered a strategic product: the European Union produces 122 million tonnes, China produces 106 million tonnes, India produces 75 million tonnes, the United States produces 56 million tonnes, Russia produces 48 million tonnes. And the United States exports 32 million tonnes, Canada exports 15 million tonnes, the European Union ten million tonnes, Argentina ten million tonnes.

As for the Arab states, all of them except Syria are importers of wheat, at their head Egypt, the land of the Nile, the largest importer of wheat in the world: Egypt 7 million tonnes; Algeria, the land of the Atlas mountains and of the farms for which it was famous in the era of the French, imports 5 million tonnes; Iraq, the land of the Tigris and Euphrates, imports 3 million tonnes; Morocco 3 million tonnes; Yemen imports nearly 3 million; Tunisia 1 of ten tonnes; and Jordan 500 thousand tonnes.

In the shadow of the decline of the dollar and the rise in the prices of oil, the cost of importing wheat will rise more and more, which will cost the budgets of those states enormous sums, even if they obtain wheat and grains at preferential prices.

This is despite what these states possess of water sources and fertile lands! Is it not abhorrent that the lands of the Nile, of the two rivers and of the Atlas mountains should be among the largest, indeed the largest, importers of wheat in the world!!!

Perhaps what came recently of recommendations in a report of the World Bank on the water sources in the Middle East and North Africa shows how the malicious policy is drawn up for the Arab states! The report concluded that in order to save water, agricultural policies must be adopted which reduce the consumption of water, so it recommended growing tomatoes and watermelons... and not growing wheat! And naturally the recommendations of the World Bank, about which Pier Francesco Mantovani, the water expert at the World Bank, said that they do not relate to technical measures decided by engineers but to deep political reforms!

This is with the knowledge that many states have the possibility of growing wheat, but the colonialist policy followed by the International Monetary Fund prevents that, as the Fund encourages the growing of tobacco and cotton in the states that follow its policy, and gives loans and aid for growing them, while it withholds loans and aid for growing wheat, in order to supply the Western factories with these two materials.

Allah has endowed the lands of the Muslims with fertile lands and abundant water, which, if well exploited, would place the Muslims in ease of living. But this needs a sound system from One Wise and All-Aware, the system of Islam, the rightly guided Khilafah, which fills the earth with justice and good. And may that be soon, by the permission of Allah.

1 Jumada al-Ula 1429 AH

Corresponding to 05/05/2008 CE
